prompt:
You are a "goldfish" reviewer: a fresh reader with no history of this project. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything.

Read only this file, plus any repository files it names (paths are relative to /home/user/maiacity):
  /home/user/maiacity/theOS/docs/aip/AIP-1.json

It is the record of one piece of planned work: building "avenCEO", an agent harness. Its definition is theOS/docs/avenceo.json; read that too (skip its "protocols" array, which only summarises outside sources).

The record's "review" field holds rounds 1 and 2 of this review, with an answer to every finding. Those findings are settled: do not raise them again unless the record shows the fix did not actually happen. Its "events" field is append-only history: older events may describe earlier revisions; judge the record as it stands now.

Your job is the comprehension test.
1. First, in your own words, write two short paragraphs (2 to 5 sentences each) under these exact headings:
   **What this proposes**
   **How the existing system works, per this record**
   If you cannot paraphrase a part, say so: that is itself a Blocker finding.
2. Then list findings. Each finding: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the affected part (field name or claim id), and what is unclear, undefined, assumed without saying, or contradictory. Look especially for: terms specific to this project that are never defined (general software terms are fine); places that assume knowledge a newcomer would not have; claims whose check would not actually catch the stated failure; contradictions between the record and avenceo.json.

Report in plain text, at most 500 words. No praise, no filler: lead with what is wrong or missing. If you find no Blocker or Major, say so plainly.

paraphrase.proposes: Build the first, smallest slice of avenCEO, all inside theOS/. It adds a check command (theOS/aven/check.mjs) that picks checks by changed path, a terms check that reads a new glossary.json of decided renames, and a headless-browser docs check. The docs check renders every view at three window sizes, fails on sideways scroll or scroll content that can't be reached, and screenshots each view. It also adds a prompt for a fresh screenshot checker and a "done rule" in theOS/CLAUDE.md. The router, the Stop hook, the metrics script and the migration of the 91 old intents are deferred. Success means three sessions with zero layout escapes, zero renamed-term escapes and fewer than ten corrections outside the gates.
paraphrase.existing: Agents check their own work, and Samuel catches layout and naming slips by looking. A static, hash-routed docs app (app.js) shows stories, the 91 intents and the avenCEO records, and works out each record's stage. Today avenCEO is a written process that the main session follows by hand. Gates pass on Samuel's chat message, quoted into the record, and spec reviews are stored in the record. Legacy tools (brain.mjs, GLOSSARY.md, check.mjs) serve only as models. I can't paraphrase what a "session" or the "work branch" is, or where the republished version is "noted".

findings.text: The parent of b1d105b39 had reachable content (the board scrolled as a whole); a reachability rule should pass there, so making it fail means tuning to the bug.
findings.note: c1 now replays only faf266961's parent; the board that scrolled as a whole is a visual break and goes to the checker (c3).

findings.text: "Changed views" is undefined; a CSS change breaks views the author did not edit; one run of a non-deterministic checker on two cases proves little.
findings.note: The pixel diff against the base commit chooses the views, not the author (c3); the checker sees every view whose pixels changed.

findings.text: "Scope" is undefined; the test misses the false-alarm case inside the rename's own scope; the renames are never listed.
findings.note: Scopes are story ids and slide text fields; the test plants each word once where the rename applies and once where its other meaning is correct; each entry cites the theOS AIP that decided it.

findings.text: Checkers also get the root CLAUDE.md and can read git log, whose messages carry the worker's reasoning.
findings.note: Partly: the root CLAUDE.md is project context, not the worker's reasoning, and it is the same for every agent. Commit messages describe changes, which a reviewer may read. c5 moved to avenCEO's rules as a practice, not a claim with a mechanical check.

findings.text: "Session" is undefined and nothing normalises for workload; Samuel's corrections are typed "answer", not "correction".
findings.note: Session defined in the glossary; the outcome counts corrections per 10 commits (baseline: 10 in 67 commits, 1.5); "correction" (Samuel corrects work called done) and "answer" (Samuel answers or redirects) are defined; avenMAIA's fix to history is an erratum.

findings.note: Viewer changes are ordinary edits under the done rule, not part of this AIP; renderRecord now handles a source-only record; stageOf reads events for the stage and review rounds only for the Specify label (derived data).
